question.problem: The volume $V$, in gallons, of water in a pool $t$ minutes after the pool starts filling can be modeled by the function $V(t)=5\sqrt{t}+2.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the water volume when $t=4$ minutes?
question.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the water volume when $t=4$ minutes is equal to ${V}^{′}(4).$

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\sqrt{t}+2) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{\frac{1}{2}}+2) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{t}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t=4,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(4) & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{4}} \\  & =\frac{5}{2(2)} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate change of the water volume when $t=4$ minutes is $\frac{5}{4}$ gallons per minute.
